prompt: A Ferris wheel has radius $15$ m and its centre sits $20$ m above the ground. A seat starts at the far right of the wheel and turns $90^\circ$. How many metres above the ground is the seat now?
hint: Height above ground $=$ centre height $+$ radius $\times \sin\theta$.

hints.text: Height above ground $=$ centre height $+$ radius $\times \sin\theta$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try the same wheel at $\theta = 0^\circ$ first. $\sin 0^\circ = 0$, so the seat is $20 + 15 \times 0 = 20$ m — level with the centre. Now redo it with $\sin 90^\circ$.

explanation: Put the centre of the wheel at the middle of a unit-circle picture. The seat rides the rim.
Its height above the centre is radius $\times \sin\theta = 15\sin\theta$, and the centre itself is $20$ m up.
At $\theta = 90^\circ$, $\sin 90^\circ = 1$, so the height is $20 + 15 \times 1 = 35$ m.

alternativeExplanations.title: No formula — just picture it
steps: A quarter turn from the far right puts the seat at the very TOP of the wheel.
The top is one radius above the centre: 20 + 15 = 35 m above the ground.

alternativeExplanations.title: Highest and lowest first
steps: The seat can never go above 20 + 15 = 35 m or below 20 − 15 = 5 m.
A 90° turn from the side reaches the peak, and the peak is 35 m.
